slides.title: Money Matters
bullets: Prepare to read, discuss and write
slides.narration: Welcome to Grade 6 English, Unit 5: Money Matters. Money is a part of everyday life, but understanding how it works is a skill that takes practice. Whether you are saving coins in a jar at home, choosing between two things you want at the market, or hearing adults talk about bills and budgets, money is always around you. In this unit, you will explore the world of financial literacy — the ability to understand and use money wisely. In this short lecture, preview the key ideas and prepare for the independent lesson.

slides.title: What you will achieve
bullets: Read and understand texts about spending, saving, and financial literacy.
Use comparative adverbs correctly to compare actions (e.g. *more quickly*, *faster*, *better*).
Use quantifiers to talk about amounts (e.g. *both*, *neither*, *some*, *many*, *a lot of*).
slides.narration: By the end of this unit, you will be able to read and understand texts about spending, saving, and financial literacy. You will also use comparative adverbs correctly to compare actions (e.g. *more quickly*, *faster*, *better*). You will also use quantifiers to talk about amounts (e.g. *both*, *neither*, *some*, *many*, *a lot of*). Keep these goals in mind as you work.

slides.title: Language for precise thinking
slides.narration: Your vocabulary work begins with these words: humble, eagerly, meagre, firmly, sensitive, uncomfortable. Listen to each pronunciation in the vocabulary lab, study its meaning in context, and use the word accurately in your own discussion and writing.

slides.title: Read critically
bullets: Money, Markets, and Making Good Choices
slides.narration: The reading sequence includes Money, Markets, and Making Good Choices and A Conversation About Saving. Read actively. Identify each text's central ideas, notice viewpoint and reliability, and support every inference with relevant evidence from the text.

slides.title: Comparative Adverbs
bullets: Comparative adverbs let us compare how two actions are done, showing that one action happens in a greater or lesser way than another, such as more quickly...
slides.narration: The first language focus is Comparative Adverbs. Comparative adverbs let us compare how two actions are done, showing that one action happens in a greater or lesser way than another, such as more quickly or faster. Notice the structure in the model examples, then apply it deliberately in connected sentences and paragraphs.

slides.title: Use English for a real purpose
bullets: Writing 1: Opinion Essay on Pocket Money
Explain, support and improve your ideas
slides.narration: In speaking, you will complete Speaking 1: Explain a Money Word. Organise your ideas, use evidence and respond clearly to questions. In writing, you will plan, draft, check and revise. Use the success criteria before submitting your work.

slides.title: You are ready to begin
bullets: Activities, quiz and optional live sessions
slides.narration: You are ready to begin. Start with the vocabulary lab, continue through reading and comprehension, apply the grammar focus, and complete the speaking and writing practices. Use the AI tutor for hints and feedback any time, and bring your questions to a live session too if you join one.
